kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the two printed tables — 4 patterns (acetaminophen/NAC repletion, the farmworker organophosphate two-family rescue with the printed 'Atropine > pralidoxime' order, the antifreeze/methanol fomepizole blockade, the methadone+ABCDEF torsades stem), 4 traps (atropine's three hats on one page, the five-metal chelator mapping, NaHCO3's two rescue logics for salicylates vs TCAs, the anticoagulant-reversal quartet with vitamin K's delay), 3 pivots (the four-move protocol, the cholinergic see-saw sorter, the reaction-names-the-mechanism router), and 8 recall cards covering all 23 antidote rows plus the 5 cardiovascular rows.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the two tables' pairings only; the attack structure, the distractor designs, and the reading protocols are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The BIND / BLOCK / REFILL / REBOOT rescue-family classification of every antidote on the page (chelation & capture; receptor competition; substrate & cofactor repletion; enzyme regeneration, metabolic blockade, detour) and the four-move reading protocol (NAME THE TOXIN → NAME THE MECHANISM OF HARM → MATCH THE RESCUE FAMILY → NAME THE ANTIDOTE AND READ ITS PUNCTUATION), including the split-row logic (organophosphates = atropine + pralidoxime; methemoglobin = methylene blue + vitamin C) and the punctuation rule (the '>' and the timing parentheses).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the 23 rows as an alphabetical association table and never asks the learner to classify the antidote by its mechanism of rescue; the four-family classification, the split-row logic, and the protocol are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms[0] + blocks[3] the list block + blocks[4] the steps block + the registry visual's Zone A lanes and Zone D protocol strip

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (BIND, BLOCK, REFILL, REBOOT / DE-FE TAKES FE / THE CHOLINERGIC SEE-SAW / K IS SLOW, FAB IS FAST). No mnemonic prints in the page's margins; First Aid's own in-cell red mnemonics (PEDS · “Penny”cillamine + trientine (3 copper pennies) · “Dimer”caprol/succ“imer” · Fomepizole (the foe of methanol) · “Meth”emoglobin→“Meth”ylene blue · “Opi”oids→Nal“oxo”ne · CASE · VANCEN [dancing] · ABCDEF “(Memorize your ABCDEF)” · the do/da/de of doxorubicin/daunorubicin/dexrazoxane) are carried ATTRIBUTED inside the verbatim table, the memory callout, and the visual, and are NOT counted among the four KYP codes.
kypExtensions.rationale: No margin mnemonic prints anywhere on pdf 269 (pdfimages + VLM census, staging-ph22/vlm-census.txt and vlm-census-bottom.txt); the four ALL-CAPS codes are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[6] the memory callout + the visual's ABCDEF band footer text

kypExtensions.summary: The organophosphate farmworker miniCase — best initial antidote — with the correct answer routing the two-family rescue (atropine = muscarinic competition first, pralidoxime = enzyme regeneration second, the printed 'Atropine > pralidoxime') and distractors inverting the order (pralidoxime monotherapy), running the see-saw backwards (physostigmine, the ANTImuscarinic row's antidote, itself an AChE inhibitor), and borrowing the right logic at the wrong receptor (naloxone, hooked by the shared pinpoint pupil).
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the pairing as one cell and never dissects the order or the two mirror rows against distractors; the vignette, the four options, and the reasoning are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: usmle.miniCase + blocks[5] the cholinergic see-saw compare

kypExtensions.summary: The five DrugCards (N-acetylcysteine, pralidoxime, fomepizole, deferoxamine + deferasirox/deferiprone, digoxin-specific antibody fragments) — one card per key antidote spanning four rescue families, each card's pairing traceable to the printed row; the antidote adverse-effect fields are explicitly marked KYP context (the source page maps toxin → antidote only and prints no antidote side effects); methylene blue is folded into blocks/recall/mnemonics rather than a drug card (documented).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source organizes the pharmacology as a toxin→treatment table, not as drug cards; the card layer is a KYP presentation, and every adverse-effect statement on the cards is flagged as KYP context rather than printed text.

CENSUS (pdfimages): ZERO raster images. VLM WAS AVAILABLE this session: ONE 120dpi glm-4.6v full-page pass (staging-ph22/vlm-census.txt) + ONE focused 2x-zoom adjudication pass on the bottom-table crop (staging-ph22/vlm-census-bottom.txt) confirmed both tables' printed row order, the color furniture (red mnemonic capitals CASE / VANCEN / PEDS / ABCDEF + Methadone's M; red in-cell mnemonics; blue titles, header rule bars, and reaction names; blue Vancomycin-infusion-reaction lead-in), and the absence of margin mnemonics and images. ADJUDICATIONS (all four independent reads agree — raw text layer, pdftotext -layout, and both VLM passes): (1) the cardiovascular table prints only TWO column headers (DRUG REACTION / CAUSAL AGENTS) — the batch brief described a NOTES column, but the print carries none; the Vancomycin infusion reaction sentence is a SECOND PARAGRAPH inside the Cutaneous flushing row's causal-agents cell — carried as printed, and the note documents the correction; (2) the batch brief's 'antiDepressa' truncation-looking worry is adjudicated NO truncation — 'antiDepressants' prints complete on one line, the wrap falls after the full word before '(eg, TCAs)'; (3) the lead row prints 'Dimercaprol, Succimer' (capital D/S — the red PEDS capitals Penicillamine/EDTA/Dimercaprol/Succimer, '(PEDS patients lead antidote)') while the arsenic and mercury rows print 'Dimercaprol, succimer' — both spellings carried as printed; (4) 'anti“C”ychotics' is the source's own printed spelling (quotation marks around the red capital C, printed example ziprasidone), and Methadone leads the torsades list OUTSIDE the ABCDEF letters.
